interpretation: The equal-length natural window reduces Angry micro-WER from 34.2% to 6.1% while retaining native Emotion2Vec Angry probability and DNSMOS quality close to the 207-code reference. This supports reference-context quality, rather than code count alone, as the main cause of the observed prefix103 failures.
limitations: This is a host screening experiment, not an RK3588 RTF measurement.
Only one speaker, one emotion, three texts and three seeds were tested.
The natural103 window is a slice of the original encoded sequence; cropped-audio re-encoding remains a useful follow-up control.
Tempo-normalized Emotion2Vec was excluded because small phase-vocoder stretches caused large classifier shifts on this matrix.
